**Sunbelt Charter Coaches — my experience on November 5**

I’m posting this because many of us use Sunbelt for airport and offsite transportation, and I don’t want another planner to go through what I did last Thursday, November 5, especially with CES bookings coming up.

I booked four coaches for a 220-person client dinner. Pickup was scheduled for 6:15 p.m. at the hotel, with transportation to a ranch venue in Henderson. The booking was confirmed in writing twice, most recently on Tuesday, November 3. Corey was the dispatcher listed on all the paperwork. I paid $8,400 total: a 50% deposit in September and the balance seven days before the event.

Only two coaches arrived. The first was 55 minutes late, and the driver said he had received the job at 5 p.m. The second broke down on the 215 with dead AC, leaving passengers on the shoulder for roughly 40 minutes. With no backup plan and no communication from Sunbelt, I put 60 people in Ubers and Lyfts on my company card, costing about $1,900.

Dinner began at 8:40 p.m. instead of 7 p.m., and the caterer charged us overtime. Two of the four paid-for coaches never arrived at all.

For context, Sunbelt handled two small airport runs for me last spring and did a great job. That history is why I trusted them with this event. I could have worked around one late bus. Having only half the booked equipment show up, with no backup or answers, is different.

Since Friday, their office line has gone to voicemail. I am still trying to get a refund for the two missing coaches and reimbursement for the rideshare costs.

My client is now reviewing whether to keep us for its March event. I hold Sunbelt responsible for putting that relationship at risk.

I’d caution other planners against using Sunbelt for anything large until they demonstrate that dispatch has been fixed. If Corey or someone from the office sees this: my refund request remains unresolved.
